paper_title: Protecting the Connectivity of a Graph Under Non-Uniform Edge Failures
classifications: Theory of computation → Design and analysis of algorithms
statement: We examine Connectivity Preservation from two perspectives. For small values of p and q, we focus on polynomial-time exact algorithms. For large values of p and q, we show hardness and devise approximation algorithms. Nonetheless, there remain some gaps between cases solvable in polynomial time and NP-hard ones. In particular, it remains open whether (1, q)-GCP admits any polynomial-time exact algorithm for constant q ≥ 3. Another interesting problem is (1, q)-GCP with q being the capacity of the minimum cuts, i.e., finding a minimum-cost edge set that intersects with all the minimum cuts. Note that for the s-t-connectivity variant, this can be tackled via Min-cost Flow techniques.
